decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar (Shadow Tag trapper). Lead Noivern+Incineroar: Tailwind plus Fake Out/Flare Blitz breaks Venusaur and Focus Sashes before sun offense rolls; under Tailwind both outspeed Scarf Krook and Unburden Hawlucha. Back: Mega Gengar traps Zard/Hawlucha (neither Ghost) and Gleams the Dark/Fighting slots; Garganacl hard-locks Zard-Y with Wide Guard + Stone Edge and shrugs WoW. This exact mode won game 1; it also covers the Krook/Sinistcha adaptation via Gleam/Shadow Ball.
decisions.notebook: Durable reads: Opp's game-1 bring was Zard-Y+Venu+Hawlucha+Sableye (sun core + disruption), leaving Krook Scarf and Sinistcha TR home — expect either as game-2 adaptation. Opp uses Sableye Fake Out + Encore to disrupt and will double-target the fast threat (Noivern took Fake Out+CC turn 3); Encore can backfire if Noivern is locked into Hurricane into Sableye. Zard clicks spread Heat Wave even into resists — it double-KO'd chipped Gengar+Noivern; never leave both chipped vs Zard. Verified tiers: Mega Gengar 200, Noivern 192; under Tailwind 400/384 beat Unburden Hawlucha 374 and Scarf Krook (237 max). Key mechanics: Hurricane 50% acc in sun — prefer Draco while sun up (turn-2 miss confirmed risk). Gengar immune to CC/Fake Out. Mega Gengar Gleam 2x SE into Hawlucha, Sableye, AND Krook; Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb SE into Sinistcha. Shadow Tag traps Zard+Hawlucha (neither Ghost). Garganacl hard-locks Zard-Y: Stone Edge guaranteed KO (confirmed: KO'd from 67% after Fake Out chip; calc 148-277% from full), survives Scorching Sands (35-49%), Wide Guard stops Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide, Purifying Salt blocks WoW; only fear sun-boosted Solar Beam. Incineroar sun Flare Blitz OHKOs Venu (confirmed turn 2). Never expose pre-Mega Gengar to Krook EQ without Tailwind. Winning line: Noivern+Incineroar lead breaks Venu, Gengar traps and Gleams, Garganacl+Incineroar closes vs Zard. Game-2 fallback if Tailwind mode loses: hard Trick Room mode with Garganacl+Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Lead Krookodile+Hawlucha: Intimidate debuffs Incineroar; Scarf Rock Slide outspeeds Noivern for chip+Sash break; Hawlucha threatens Incineroar with Close Combat or Taunts Noivern. Sableye is dead weight vs Dark Incineroar. Back Charizard-Y+Venusaur form sun mode for endgame after disruptors have done their job.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Incineroar+Noivern, using Fake Out turn 1 and switching Incineroar out to reuse Intimidate. Garganacl is a bulky Rock with Wide Guard and Stone Edge, saved for endgame. Gengar is a fast special attacker. They did not bring Kingambit or Hatterene game 1, but may bring Trick Room mode in future games. Our Charizard-Y must avoid Stone Edge and Fake Out; Scorching Sands is key. Venusaur is threatened by Noivern's Hurricane. Sableye cannot use Prankster status moves on Dark-type Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) flinches Krook regardless of its 184-237 speed roll, removing Rock Slide/EQ spread. Noivern (192) always precedes Hawlucha (151-187), so Tailwind resolves before Taunt lands. Hawlucha's lone CC at -1 Atk is ~43-78% (calc 65-117 ignores the drop) — Incineroar survives + Sitrus. Turn 2 under Tailwind: Noivern 384 beats Unburden Hawlucha 374 and Scarf Krook 237; Hurricane pops the sash, Incineroar cleans up.
decisions.notebook: Durable reads: Opp's game-1 bring was Zard-Y+Venu+Hawlucha+Sableye; game-2 leads Krook-Scarf+Hawlucha — bench still holds Zard/Venu/Sableye/Sinistcha, expect Sableye Fake Out+Encore disruption and Zard spread Heat Wave late; never leave both my mons chipped vs Zard. Encore can backfire if Noivern locked into Hurricane into Sableye. Verified tiers: Mega Gengar 200, Noivern 192; under Tailwind 400/384 beat Unburden Hawlucha 374 and Scarf Krook 237 max. Hurricane 50% acc in sun — prefer Draco while sun up. Gengar immune to CC/Fake Out; Mega Gleam 2x SE into Hawlucha/Sableye/Krook; Shadow Tag traps Zard+Hawlucha. Garganacl hard-locks Zard-Y (Stone Edge KO, Wide Guard stops Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide, Purifying Salt blocks WoW; fears only sun Solar Beam). Incineroar sun Flare Blitz OHKOs Venu. Never expose pre-Mega Gengar to Krook EQ without Tailwind. Game-2 plan: Tailwind up turn 1 (done), Hurricane pops Hawlucha sash turn 2, then Gengar traps and Garganacl+Incineroar close vs Zard. Fallback if Tailwind mode loses: hard Trick Room with Garganacl+Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide spreads 29-53% on Noivern and 25-46% on Incineroar; Taunt denies Tailwind if Hawlucha isn't Fake Out'd. When Fake Out hits Krookodile, Taunt still lands (speed uncertain but Noivern locked into attacks afterward). When Fake Out hits Hawlucha, Rock Slide still chips both. Either way we get one action through. Noivern Hurricane OHKOs Hawlucha but Sash holds, activating Unburden for future speed advantage.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Incineroar+Noivern, uses Fake Out turn 1 and switches Incineroar to recycle Intimidate. Garganacl is bulky Wide Guard/Stone Edge endgame. Gengar is fast special attacker. They didn't bring Kingambit or Hatterene game 1 but may bring Trick Room later. Charizard-Y must avoid Stone Edge; Scorching Sands key. Venusaur threatened by Noivern Hurricane.

decisions.rationale: Double into Krookodile: Draco (90%) + Flare Blitz KOs from 73% on any hit rolls, eliminating the Scarf Rock Slide/EQ threat before Gengar enters (EQ is 2x on Gengar). Incineroar survives -1 Rock Slide + CC via Sitrus; Noivern's sash absorbs Rock Slide. Leaving Hawlucha full is fine: Noivern (384) outspeeds even Unburden (374 max), Hurricane/Gleam are 2x SE, and Mega Gengar traps it later.

G2 plan: Krook removed t2, then Noivern/Gengar handle Hawlucha, Garganacl+Incineroar close vs Zard/Venu. Fallback if Tailwind mode loses: hard Trick Room with Garganacl+Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Switching Krookodile to Charizard avoids PartingShot debuff while Hawlucha blocks Hurricane. Charizard takes neutral Hurricane if targeted (26-76%) and FlareBlitz is NVE. Next turn Mega Charizard-Y sets Sun, enabling Venusaur Chlorophyll endgame. Staying in risks Shadow Tag Gengar trap and Krookodile at -2 Atk being dead weight.

Double-target Hawlucha while it's -1 and Protect-nerfed. Draco (90% acc regardless of sun) + Flare Blitz KOs through sash in the large majority of rolls vs a min-bulk Jolly Sash Hawlucha, and every likely switch-in (Krook/Venu/Sableye) gets KO'd or crippled. Only beaten by a 33% Protect. Incineroar survives any single hit; even a perfect opposing double trades Hawlucha for it, leaving Garganacl+Gengar to close vs 72% Zard.

decisions.rationale: Gengar is the plan: it Megas next turn for Shadow Tag, trapping Zard+Hawlucha before they can pivot (switch phase precedes Mega, but they must guess the switch-in). Verified: Mega Gengar survives Zard Scorching Sands (max 85.9%), and Shadow Ball takes 28.6-57.5% off Zard, so Noivern Draco + Shadow Ball cleans Zard after Noivern KOs 12% Hawlucha first (384 Spe). Gengar is immune to Hawlucha CC and Sableye Fake Out. Garganacl stays benched as the endgame Zard lock; bringing it now lets Zard pivot

decisions.rationale: Charizard must Protect to avoid Hurricane OHKO range (69-105%) and safely Mega Evolve. Hawlucha Close Combat pressures Incineroar; if Hurricane breaks sash, Unburden activates (374 Speed) and Acrobatics doubles to 110 BP next turn. Opponent likely Parting Shots rather than double-targeting since they value Intimidate cycling. Sun comes up for Charizard-Y on turn 4 even if Hawlucha goes down.
decisions.notebook: Opponent leads Incineroar+Noivern both games: Fake Out turn 1, Tailwind turn 1, then Incineroar Parting Shots to cycle Intimidate. Noivern carries Focus Sash and is Taunt-vulnerable. Garganacl is Wide Guard/Stone Edge endgame. Gengar-Mega is Shadow Tag trapper. Kingambit and Hatterene not seen game 1; may bring Trick Room later. Charizard-Y must avoid Stone Edge; sun activates after Mega. Venusaur threatened by Noivern Hurricane. Plan: Mega Evolve Charizard safely, activate sun, sweep with Venusaur late-game.

decisions.rationale: Gleam+Draco covers every branch: Hawlucha dies unless Protect, a Krook switch eats 64-120% (~80% KO), and if Zard stays it falls to ~26-46%, where next turn Gengar (200) and Noivern (192) outspeed Zard (max 167) even after Tailwind ends and finish it. Hawlucha can't threaten either mon (CC immune vs Gengar, Acro weak), so spread coverage beats doubling Zard, which loses to the Krook switch.

Hawlucha is low threat vs Gengar+Noivern (CC immune, Acro weak) — safe to ignore as damage. G2 plan: trap with Gengar, Gleam+Draco coverage, Garganacl endgame lock; fallback hard Trick Room with Garganacl.

decisions.rationale: Hawlucha at 12% is dead weight; switching to Venusaur now gets Chlorophyll online before Tailwind ends. Noivern at -2 SpA with 50% accurate Hurricane is low-threat. Heat Wave in sun pressures both foes and can OHKO Gengar before it Mega Evolves. Next turn Venusaur outspeeds everything, and Charizard+Venusaur sun core dominates.

Venusaur Chlorophyll + sun is primary win condition. Noivern Draco Meteor PP likely depleted (used 2). Charizard Protect used once — success rate reduced.

decisions.rationale: Gengar dies to any hit (Heat Wave or LO Earth Power both KO from 19%), so Protect is mandatory. Re-setting Tailwind is the only way Gengar (400) ever outspeeds Chlorophyll Venusaur (max 290): T6 Shadow Ball + Draco combine ~51-111% into 84% Venusaur, likely removing the Garganacl counter while foes stay trapped by Shadow Tag. Even if Sleep Powder lands on Noivern, Tailwind is set and Gengar still gets one big hit. Tailwind also restores speed control vs Scarf Krookodile later.

G2 plan executed: Tailwind reset + Gengar Protect; T6 double into Venusaur under Tailwind, then Garganacl endgame lock on Zard with Wide Guard vs Krook EQ.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur outspeeds everything at 290 Speed. Sleep Powder on Noivern removes the only real threat to Venusaur (Hurricane 2x) before it moves. Charizard Heat Wave pressures both foes: likely KOs 18% Gengar if it doesn't Protect, breaks Noivern's Sash. Even on miss, Venusaur survives Sludge Bomb + weakened Hurricane. Gengar at 18% is forced to Protect or risk dying, limiting its options.

decisions.rationale: Both actives die to EP+Heat Wave regardless, so max EV is making Gengar's likely-final move count: Sludge Bomb (36.4-80%, 30% poison) into Venusaur, the only mon that beats Garganacl. If Noivern wakes (1/3), added Draco (18-39%) can outright KO Venu from 84%. Switching Garganacl in just gets it ground down by LO Earth Power (37-83%) with Solar Beam risk. If Venu is crippled, Garganacl wins the endgame: guaranteed Stone Edge OHKO on Zard, Wide Guard for Krook EQ/Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Durable reads: Opp g1 bring Zard-Y+Venu+Hawlucha+Sableye; g2 Krook-Scarf+Hawlucha+Zard+Venu. Expect Sableye FakeOut+Encore disruption g3; Zard spread Heat Wave late. Verified tiers: Mega Gengar 200, Noivern 192; under Tailwind 400/384 beat Chlorophyll Venu (max 290), Unburden Hawlucha (max 374), Scarf Krook (max 237); WITHOUT Tailwind Scarf Krook outspeeds both. Sim quirk: missed/Protect-blocked Draco does NOT drop SpA. Shadow Tag traps foes only while Gengar on field; Gengar itself can switch. New verified calcs: Zard sun spread Heat Wave does ~40% to Noivern THROUGH resist (KOs below ~40%); Mega Gengar Sludge Bomb into Venu 36.4-80% (beats Shadow Ball 32.6-71.6%, +30% poison); Venu LO Earth Power into Garganacl 37.2-82.9% — Garganacl CANNOT switch into Venu+Zard (EP+HW ~55-122%, EP+Solar Beam lethal); Garganacl Stone Edge = guaranteed OHKO on Zard-Y at any HP. Endgame rules: kill/cripple Venu BEFORE Garganacl enters (target <=45% so Stone Edge finishes); Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide but NOT Earth Power/CC; Krook CC 2x SE is the endgame threat — grind with Salt Cure chip + Leftovers. Purifying Salt blocks Sleep Powder/WoW. G3 plan: consider leading Gengar+Noivern for immediate Tailwind+pressure, keep Garganacl+Incineroar back; never let Krook in healthy vs Gengar without Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Only Garganacl remains; it must fill one slot and the other passes. Plan: Stone Edge Charizard-Y immediately (verified guaranteed OHKO) to remove the sun abuser with SE coverage, use Protect/Wide Guard to stall the last 2 sun turns, then Salt Cure + Stone Edge Venusaur (already at 44%). Purifying Salt blocks Sleep Powder. Krookodile is the final hurdle — grind with Salt Cure chip + Leftovers.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur outspeeds all under Chlorophyll. Earth Power guarantees OHKO on 18% Gengar-Mega (55-104% range). Sun-boosted Heat Wave guarantees OHKO on 18% Noivern (25-47%, no Sash activation). If Gengar Protects, Noivern still falls; if it doesn't, both are KO'd before they act. Cleanest path to 2v0.
decisions.notebook: Noivern: Draco Meteor PP 0 (used 3), Focus Sash intact but HP below threshold, Tailwind used. Gengar-Mega: Shadow Tag confirmed, Protect used once (reduced). Back row: Kingambit (BlackGlasses, Defiant, Brave), Hatterene (MentalHerb, MagicBounce, Quiet, Trick Room threat), Garganacl (Leftovers, PurifyingSalt, WideGuard). Sun has 2 turns remaining. Venusaur Chlorophyll sweep is primary win condition; preserve Charizard for Sun reset potential. Hawlucha Sash consumed, Unburden active.

decisions.rationale: EP + Solar Beam = ~95-197% combined and Garganacl always moves last (55 Spe), so any attack faints it before it acts. Protect (+4 priority, confirmed first) blocks both, ends the sun (no instant Solar Beam, Chlorophyll off, Heat Wave unboosted), and preserves the Stone Edge OHKO on Zard for next turn. Wide Guard fails vs single-target EP/SB/SS.

Garganacl CANNOT tank Venu+Zard doubles — Protect to burn sun, then Stone Edge Zard. Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave/EQ/Rock Slide only, NOT EP/CC/Solar Beam/SS/Giga Drain. decisions.rationale: Garganacl is the last foe. PurifyingSalt blocks Sleep Powder. Charizard Protects to scout; Venusaur outspeeds (290 vs 55-87) and Giga Drain has a chance to OHKO (58.5-104%). If Garganacl Protects, we lose little. If it attacks, Charizard is safe and Venusaur either KOs or softens for Charizard's Scorching Sands finish next turn.
decisions.notebook: Noivern: Draco Meteor PP 0, Focus Sash intact, Tailwind used. Gengar-Mega: Shadow Tag, Protect used once (reduced). Garganacl: Leftovers, PurifyingSalt (blocks sleep/status), WideGuard, Protect unused (100% success), Stone Edge + Salt Cure. Back row Kingambit and Hatterene not brought. Sun expires after this turn. Venusaur Chlorophyll sweep remains primary win condition; preserve Charizard for Sun reset potential. Hawlucha Sash consumed, Unburden active. Up 1-0 in series.

decisions.rationale: Salt Cure into Charizard is 100% accurate and guarantees the KO: min roll 55.1% plus 12.5% end-of-turn residual exceeds its 58% HP, beating Stone Edge's 80% reliability. From full HP I survive any single hit (EP max 82.9%); only a double-up KOs me, and Protect is just 33%, so attacking is best and resets my Protect counter to full for next turn vs Venusaur. Removing the Mega/sun-setter is the top priority.

decisions.rationale: Both outspeed Garganacl and attack before it moves. Scorching Sands (38-70%) + Giga Drain (58-104%) gives 96-174% combined; even with Leftovers, KO is highly probable. If they survive, Charizard may fall to Stone Edge, but Venusaur cleans up with Giga Drain next turn. Ends the game fastest and minimizes risk.

reflections.summary: The opponent's team of Gengar-Mega, Noivern, Incineroar, and Garganacl lacked a reliable answer to the Charizard-Venusaur sun core. Venusaur's Earth Power and Giga Drain covered Gengar and Garganacl, while Sleep Powder disabled Noivern. The absence of Trick Room allowed our speed advantage to dominate, and the opponent failed to use Wide Guard effectively.
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, expect the opponent to bring Hatterene for Trick Room and Kingambit for priority. Lead Hawlucha to Taunt Hatterene or double-target it to prevent Trick Room. Use single-target moves like Scorching Sands and Giga Drain to bypass Garganacl's Wide Guard instead of relying on Heat Wave.
reflections.notebook: Game 2: Opponent brought Gengar-Mega (Dazzling Gleam, Shadow Tag), Noivern (Draco Meteor, Hurricane, Tailwind, Protect, possibly Taunt), Incineroar (Fake Out, Flare Blitz, Throat Chop, Parting Shot), Garganacl (Salt Cure, Stone Edge, Wide Guard, Protect). Gengar-Mega and Noivern are fast and frail. Garganacl is bulky with Wide Guard but did not use it effectively. Sun expired turn 7. Venusaur's Earth Power and Giga Drain were key. Series tied 1-1. Opponent likely to bring Hatterene (Trick Room, Mental Herb) and Kingambit (Sucker Punch, Defiant, Black Glasses) in game 3. Prepare for Trick Room; Taunt or double-target Hatterene.
